//: WHERE EACH LAYER'S CODE LIVES, in ONE place, at the ROOT since `a11ign/control` took `packages/control` (#3506): a file inside a directory that is laid and untracked cannot pin its own tag, and `scripts/lay-layer.mjs` reads THIS file to lay it and listed here by hand rather than discovered by glob (ADR 0039 item 6, #3394). `path` is relative to the repository root this checkout is. Both layers have their own repository (`remote`): `nvda-worker` since #3447, `screenreader-fleet` since #3504 (its repository keeps the directory at the same path, so `path` names both ends), and a host holds a checkout of each at `path`; the core's CI and a worktree get `screenreader-fleet`'s `src/` from `scripts/lay-layer.mjs`, at the tag its lockfile entry pins. A layer that lives in its OWN repository also declares `remote` (its clone URL, https, ending .git) and optionally `branch` (default main): that is what makes a guest hold a second checkout of it at `path`, pinned to its own commit beside the core's (`--layer-ref`, #3395). A host that has run `pnpm install` holds such a layer LAID rather than cloned (`scripts/lay-layer.mjs` replaces the clone with `src/` and `.layer-ref`, no `.git`), and the lab's and a guest's checks accept that shape and no other tree at `path` (#3819). A layer with no `remote` is inside the core checkout and a guest needs nothing more. Read through `src/layer-checkouts.mjs`, never by hand. `package` (#3939) is the part of the registry name after `@a11ign/` when it is NOT the layer's key: `nvda-worker` is `@a11ign/screenreader-worker`, and `lay-layer.mjs` reads the declaration rather than inferring the package from the key; a layer without it is `@a11ign/<key>`. A layer that is NOT held on a host but only LAID for the core's own tests and scripts is declared under `pinned` instead, never under `layers` (#3505): `lab` is `private: true` and never on a registry, so it has no lockfile entry to read, and its `tag` is the pin, a `v<semver>` and never a branch. It is kept out of `layers` because a layer declared there with a `remote` is one every guest and every lab job must hold a pinned checkout of (`separateLayers`, `--layer-ref`, `layer_refs`), and nothing on a worker runs the lab; a host gets `packages/lab` from `pnpm install` (`prepare` runs `scripts/lay-layer.mjs lab`). `lays` names what of it is laid when that is more than `src/`: the lab's root scripts, its baselines, `rule-ownership.json` and its `CLAUDE.md` are read by path from the rest of the tree (the agent-org tool's own tests read the last). Moving `lab`'s tag is a change HERE, in the same pull request as whatever needed the newer tree. `control` is the third pinned layer (#3506) and the odd one: the code that READS this declaration is the layer itself, so `declares` names the file inside the laid layer that is a COPY of this one (`lay-layer.mjs` writes it, over whatever the tag holds, so the two cannot differ), and `keeps` names files an operator keeps beside the layer's own (an untracked `inventory.yml`, a `*.local.yml`), which a re-lay carries across rather than deleting. Moving `control`'s tag is a change HERE and nowhere else.
